notable_absence.finding: The page never mentions DCP (protocol:dcp) at all, despite change history being conceptually adjacent to mutation streaming (it records the same mutation stream to disk that DCP would relay live). The only mechanism named for reading change-history contents is the Kafka Connector, not a DCP client. This looks like a real documentation gap rather than a deliberate distinction: the page gives no architectural account of how mutations get into the change history in the first place (whether via the same internal path DCP uses, or a separate write path inside Magma).

cross_component_finding: Change history is stated as available only 'when Magma storage is used for a bucket' - the page never states the converse (that Couchstore buckets cannot have change history), but no enablement path is offered for Couchstore either, and storage-engine:couchstore is the only other storage-engine concept in the registry. This is an implicit, not stated, exclusivity - flagged rather than asserted as a doesNotSupport relation, since the page phrases it only positively.
cross_product_finding: No cross-product angle on this page: change history/CDC is a pure Couchbase Server + Magma capability, surfaced only through the REST API, couchbase-cli, cbstats and the Kafka Connector - no Capella, SDK, or mobile angle appears anywhere on the page.
